what: Dropbox stores files in the cloud and syncs them across devices. It also sells Dropbox Sign for electronic signatures and DocSend for sharing documents with tracking.
customers: Individuals, freelancers and small teams paying monthly or annual subscriptions.
money: storage and collaboration plans for individuals and teams
moat: Hundreds of millions of files already stored, synced into people's folder habits and shared links, which makes moving to another service a chore few users undertake.
risks: Revenue has been flat at $2.5B for three years: this is not a growing business
Google and Microsoft bundle storage into subscriptions customers already pay for
Paying user numbers have started to decline
opportunities: 8.3 times free cash flow with $915M of free cash flow against a $7.6B market value
A 20.2% net margin and relentless share buybacks, which have cut the share count sharply
watch: Paying user count and free cash flow per share, which buybacks keep lifting.
